# Add an action or a check

**The finished shape:** `src/main/java/com/playwrightplayground/tests/pages/networkmocking/` (the page, its elements and actions) and `src/test/java/com/playwrightplayground/tests/cases/NetworkMockingFormTest.java`, the suite's worked example (README.md, "Write a test"). What follows is only what to add.

The crawl's own are already there: every button, field and dropdown it saw with a locator it
trusts is in the page's Elements, above the YOURS block, with a method that uses it
(`enter().email(...)`, `click().send()`, a `fill...Form(...)` task). Add one here only for what the
crawl did not see (it appears after a click, behind a login, after a form is sent), or for a fragile
one controls/<Page>.md lists and says why.

A page has a class per door it needs, in `pages/<type>/actions/` (read and verify always; the others
when the crawl saw something for them, or you added one). Each has a YOURS block for its methods. A
door a page lacks: add its interface (`EnterableAction<...EnterActions>`) to the page class's YOURS
**extras** block with the door's method, and the class beside the others, copied from a page that has one:

| Door | Class | Method returns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `click()` | `...ClickActions` | the next page if the click changes page, else `this` |
| `enter()` | `...EnterActions` | `this` |
| `check()` / `uncheck()` | `...CheckActions` | `this` (one method serves both: it gets `check`) |
| `clear()` | `...ClearActions` (only if you add one: fields are emptied in `enter()`, `clearEmail()`) | `this` |
| `read()` | `...ReadActions` | the value |
| `verify()` | `...VerifyActions` | `this` |
| `execute()` | `...Tasks` | a sequence of steps a story names, one method each (add-a-task.md) |
| `navigateTo()` | `HeaderNavigableActions` (the header and footer) | the page the menu link leads to, from any page |

Every click, enter, check and clear class also has `verify()`, so a chain goes on to its checks from there
(`.enter().email("a@b.c").verify().holds(...)`); a class you add needs one too.

Name each method for what a visitor does or sees (`signUp()`, `email(text)`, `showsThanks()`),
never for the element's technology (`clickButton2()`). Build it from the library, one line:

```java
    public HomeClickActions acceptTerms() {
        UserActions.click(page, HomeElements.ACCEPT_BUTTON);
        return this;
    }

    /** Sends the form; the thank-you page comes next. */
    public ThanksPage submit() {
        UserActions.click(page, HomeElements.SUBMIT_BUTTON);
        return new ThanksPage(page).get();
    }

    public HomeVerifyActions showsThanks() {
        Checks.isShown(page, HomeElements.THANKS_HEADING);
        return this;
    }
```

The library logs each step in plain English and waits for the element. When nothing in it fits,
log the step yourself with `StepLog.step("...")` before doing it, and wait with `WaitActions`,
never `Thread.sleep`. A click that leads to another page returns `new NextPage(page).get()`,
which waits until that page has fully loaded; import that page class in the file's **imports**
YOURS block (`import com.playwrightplayground.tests.pages.<type>.NextPage;`) if the file does not import it already. Every
import you add goes there, the library's too (`WaitActions`, `Checks`, `StepLog`): an import written
among the generated ones is a change outside YOURS, and SuiteRulesTest (SR-16) fails the build on it.

Every verify() already has `shows(element)`, `doesNotShow(element)`, `says(element, text)`,
`showsText(text)`, `isEmpty(field)` and `refusesEmpty(field)` (the browser will not send the form
with that required field empty; nothing is sent to find out). Add a named check when the story's words say more than that (`showsThanks()`
reads better than `shows(HomeElements.THANKS_HEADING)`).
